jobs.title: Technical Product Marketing Engineer, Robotics Simulation - New College Grad 2027
jobs.description: Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world! We are looking for a Technical Product Marketing Engineer to build robotics simulation workflows and demonstrate how AI models can solve robotics tasks. You will develop working examples, evaluate their behavior and performance, and turn your findings into practical resources that help developers understand and adopt NVIDIA robotics technologies. As part of NVIDIA’s Robotics Technical Marketing team, you will work with engineering, product management, and product marketing to connect technical capabilities with developer needs. You will own well-defined projects—from implementation and testing through demonstrations and technical content—with mentorship and technical review from experienced teammates. What you will be doing: Develop and test robotics simulation w/ agentic workflows using NVIDIA platforms Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab, including configuring robot models, environments, sensors, and task scenarios. Integrate AI models and robot policies into simulation workflows, connecting simulation inputs, model inference, and robot behavior. Build reusable Python code and sample applications that demonstrate practical robotics use cases. Evaluate task success, runtime performance, and failure cases through repeatable experiments; document configurations, results, and limitations. Create demos, tutorials, technical blogs, and workflow guides that explain what you built, how it works, and how developers can reproduce the results. Collaborate with engineering and product teams to troubleshoot integration issues, validate technical claims, and surface opportunities to improve the developer experience. Present your work and contribute to technical demonstrations and educational materials for developers, partners, and customer-facing teams. What we need to see: Pursuing or recently completed a BS or MS degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience. Strong Python programming fundamentals, including experience debugging, testing, and organizing code. Hands-on academic, research, internship, or personal project experience with robotics or simulation. Foundational understanding of linear algebra, coordinate transformations, and robotics concepts such as sensors, kinematics, or control. Familiarity with machine learning fundamentals and practical experience running or evaluating models using a framework such as PyTorch. Ability to investigate technical problems systematically and communicate results through clear writing and presentations. Initiative in learning new tools, incorporating feedback, and following through on defined technical deliverables. Relevant experience may come from coursework, capstone projects, research, internships, open-source contributions, or personal projects. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Experience with NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, or other robotics simulators. A project applying learned policies or pre-trained AI models to robotics tasks, such as perception, manipulation, or navigation. Exposure to reinforcement learning, imitation learning, synthetic data generation, or simulation-to-real evaluation. Familiarity with Linux, Git, ROS 2, C++, or GPU-accelerated computing. Examples of reusable code, demonstrations, tutorials, or technical presentations that make a complex topic understandable and help others reproduce your work. NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you! Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 84,000 USD - 143,750 USD for Level 1, and 100,000 USD - 161,000 USD for Level 2. You will also be eligible for equity and benefits . Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 23, 2026. This posting is for an existing vacancy. NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes. NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Data Engineer, Amazon Live Data Engineering, Sciences and Analytics (DESA)
jobs.description: Description Amazon Live is building the future of shoppable video — connecting brands with customers through livestreams, short-form video, and creator-driven content across Amazon Shopping, Fire TV, Prime Video, and social platforms. The product serves millions of monthly viewers, processes billions of events daily across 9 marketplaces, and generates tens of millions of dollars in advertiser revenue, with a goal to reach 100MM+ MAUs and 20K+ brands in the next couple of years. Amazon Live has a mature, high-performing data platform powering reporting across 9 marketplaces, 14+ dashboards, real-time creator analytics, and a growing suite of AI-native tooling (self-serve analytics agents, agentic operational assistants). The opportunity ahead is to build the next layer on that strong foundation: the team is standing up an intelligence layer — causal measurement, content intelligence, and ranking signals — and that requires a new class of foundational, reusable data assets purpose-built for both analytics and ML consumption. This role builds them. We are looking for a Data Engineer to join the DESA team as a dedicated owner of forward-looking data architecture. You will design and build durable, well-modeled datasets that serve three consumers at once: the BIE for executive reporting, the Applied Scientists for model training, and downstream ML systems (ranking, personalization, recommendations) for feature consumption. The goal is leverage — build an asset once, serve many use cases, and let the whole team move faster on top of it. Your work becomes the foundation the science function builds on: when the data assets are ready ahead of need, scientists model from day one instead of waiting on bespoke pipelines. This is a high-ownership role on a team that moves fast. You will go from problem to production quickly, in a challenging and fast-paced environment, and you will work across the full breadth of the data domain — platform engineering, data modeling, ML-ready feature production, data quality, and AI-assisted development. You will partner closely with Applied Scientists, MLEs, fellow Data Engineers, and the BIE, giving you the opportunity to learn and execute across every aspect of a modern data organization — from raw event ingestion through the models and reporting that move multi-million-dollar business decisions. Key job responsibilities - Design and build a content metadata layer that unifies broadcast events, product catalog data, creator profiles, and show metadata into reusable assets consumed by both dashboards and models. - Build cross-session shopper profile datasets that sessionize event data across visits and compute rolling engagement metrics (frequency, recency, depth, conversion lag). - Build integration pipelines connecting retail catalog and advertising performance data into the Amazon Live platform, unlocking new dimensions for analytics and ML. - Produce structured, ML-ready datasets that feed Applied Scientists' models and serve features to downstream ranking and personalization systems. - Own and advance data quality: proactive monitoring and anomaly detection so the team stays ahead of issues. - Advance platform engineering maturity — CI/CD for ETL (BDT/Maestro), standardized deployment, and AI-assisted code generation and review. - Partner with Applied Scientists, MLEs, DEs, and the BIE to align data assets to model, serving, and reporting needs. A day in the life You will move fast across a broad surface. Some weeks you will be designing a denormalized content metadata asset with an Applied Scientist to unblock a new model; other weeks you will be integrating a retail or advertising data source, hardening a pipeline's CI/CD, building data-quality alarms, or packaging features for the distribution team's ranking systems. You will partner daily with scientists, MLEs, DEs, and the BIE — scoping what to build and how it will be consumed — and you will have self-serve analytics agents and agentic operational tooling to accelerate your work (and a hand in extending that tooling as the platform grows). The pace is quick, the problems span the full data lifecycle, and the ownership is real. About the team The DESA team owns the data platform, analytics, and sciences for Amazon Live and Shop the Show. It is a compact, senior, high-trust team: DEs own the infrastructure and foundational data assets, the BIE owns executive reporting, Applied Scientists and MLEs own the models, experiments, and signals that turn data into product value, and everyone collaborates closely across those boundaries. As a Data Engineer here, you own forward-looking data architecture — the durable, reusable foundation the intelligence layer is built on — and you get exposure to the entire data domain, from event ingestion through production ML and leadership reporting. Your datasets become shared org infrastructure: the inputs to attribution models for partner teams, ranking features for distribution, and the reporting the business runs on. - 3+ years of data engineering experience - Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines - Experience with SQL - Experience with AWS technologies like Redshift, S3, AWS Glue, EMR, Kinesis, FireHose, Lambda, and IAM roles and permissions - Experience with non-relational databases / data stores (object storage, document or key-value stores, graph databases, column-family databases) Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Measurement, Ad Tech, and Data Science (MADS) Foundations- Traffic
jobs.description: Amazon Ads Traffic ingests hundreds of billions of ad events daily, decorates them with dimensional and identity data, and publishes the structured traffic and billing datasets that the entire Ads measurement ecosystem depends on — including three of the five critical metrics used for Ads billing. You'll design and deliver features across Spark-based EMR pipelines, decoration jobs, and publication systems that operate under strict tier-one SLAs for data freshness and accuracy. The Traffic Applications team, part of Measurement, AdTech, and Data Science (MADS), is the first system in the MADS stack to encounter regulatory and identity changes — meaning the architectural decisions made here propagate across the entire measurement pipeline. You'll work on high-visibility initiatives that directly impact Ads VP and SVP-level goals, including compliance work (GDPR, ePrivacy), geo-targeting features, and architecture scalability to support spiky traffic from live sports events. Key job responsibilities - Design and develop features across Spark-based EMR pipelines, decoration jobs, and publication systems that process hundreds of billions of ad events daily - Deliver end to end across the full development lifecycle — from requirements and system design through implementation, testing, deployment, and operations under tier-one SLAs - Navigate technical problems with competing constraints — regulatory deadlines, performance requirements, cost targets, and cross-org dependencies — and propose well-reasoned solutions - Collaborate with engineers across Ads, Customer Trust, and identity-owning upstream systems to ensure Traffic's design decisions support downstream consumers - Contribute to compliance initiatives (GDPR, ePrivacy) and scalability efforts for high-traffic events like live sports - Maintain sound operational practices — alarms, telemetry, runbooks — for a system where data freshness and accuracy directly impact billing - Mentor peers through design reviews, code reviews, and knowledge sharing A day in the life On a typical day you might start with a stand-up to align on priorities, then dive into building or extending a Spark pipeline to handle a new decoration requirement. After lunch, you could be debugging a data freshness issue against a tier-one SLA, tracing it through the ingestion path to a root cause. Between coding, you'll review pull requests, participate in design discussions for upcoming compliance or scalability work, and collaborate with downstream consumers to understand how they use your datasets. About the team The Traffic Applications team owns the data ingress system for all of Amazon Ads — ingesting hundreds of billions of ad events daily, decorating them with dimensional and identity data, and publishing structured traffic and billing datasets to consumers across the Ads ecosystem. The system operates under strict SLAs for data freshness and accuracy on tier-one advertising metrics, owning three of the five metrics used for billing. jobs.description: Who We Are Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology. What We Offer Salary: $104,000.00 - $143,000.00 Location: Santa Clara,CA You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more. At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits . As a Software Engineer at Applied Materials, you’ll dive deep into ground-breaking technologies—like machine learning and AI—to craft novel software solutions that solve our customers’ high-value problems. Our Software Engineers are responsible for designing, prototyping, developing, and debugging software solutions for semiconductor equipment components and devices to ensure quality and functionality. You'll develop software documentation and test procedures, troubleshoot software problems, and communicate with internal customers to understand project requirements. As part of our team, you'll contribute your expertise in intricate systems, deciphering code, and anticipating software behaviors to ensure Applied remains the leader in the semiconductor and display sectors.
